subject: Hybrid endpoint SLA: TTFT vs Sustained Tokens for Quantic Pilot
messages:
From: Elena Moretti <elena.moretti@quanticai.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@quanticai.com
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot SLA questions — TTFT and tokens/sec expectations

Hi Michael and Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Quantic integration team is excited to move to a short pilot (4 weeks) to validate streaming behavior for our real-time summarization UI. Before we lock schedules, two quick SLA items we need clarity on:

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming endpoints: our UX team expects a visible first token within 120ms for 90th percentile under the pilot workload (single-user interactive, avg prompt length ~120 tokens). Is that an achievable objective on your hosted hybrid endpoints?

2) Sustained token throughput: while TTFT is important for perceived responsiveness, we also want a token/sec expectation for sustained backfills where multiple concurrent streams (up to 8 concurrent sessions) will run for 30–60s. Can you provide a conservative tokens/sec guarantee or guidance for the pilot region (eu-west-1)?

We’ve attached our pilot_requirements.pdf with sample traces and a short ops contact (ops@quanticai.com). If you can send a short SLA carveout note we can share with procurement.

Best,
Elena
Director, Integrations
QuanticAI

---

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moretti <elena.moretti@quanticai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA questions — TTFT and tokens/sec expectations

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and for the traces. We can support a narrow, pilot-scoped SLA that covers both TTFT and a conservative sustained throughput expectation, with a few carveouts. Quick summary of our proposal:

- TTFT (streaming endpoints): Target 90th percentile TTFT <= 150ms in eu-west-1 for single-interactive sessions that match the pilot prompt distribution. We’ll instrument and report TTFT per-request in the Console during the pilot.

- Sustained tokens/sec: For up to 8 concurrent streams of ~30–60s, we propose a conservative guideline of 1200 tokens/sec aggregate (approx 150 tokens/sec per session). This is a pilot commitment — not a contractual peak SLA — and includes an autoburst buffer for brief spikes.

- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: If capacity is constrained, we will automatically route to a compatible quantized model variant (preserving semantics) that keeps TTFT latency within 300ms 90th pct and sustains lower throughput with progressive shedding. We will give you 24-hour notice before switching variants for planned maintenance.

I’ve looped in Stephanie and Marissa for the draft service-level wording and procurement language. Attaching a one-page carveout doc and the Service_Levels_Draft_v2 for your review.

Next steps: 1) confirm you can accept the pilot-scoped TTFT and aggregate tokens/sec guideline, 2) we’ll timebox the variant fallback behavior in the pilot runbook, and 3) sign the pilot addendum.

Thanks —
Michael
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA questions — TTFT and tokens/sec expectations

Couple of notes for procurement/legal:

- Language should make clear this is a pilot-scoped operational objective (performance guidance) with metrics captured during the pilot. Don’t present the 1200 tokens/sec as a full commercial throughput SLA — classify as "pilot performance commitment".

- Add a clause for model variant fallback that requires notification within 24 hours and an explicit post-mortem if we trigger a fallback more than twice in the pilot window.

- For TTFT, avoid hard 90th percentile contractual thresholds; instead commit to reporting and a remediation path that includes a credits schedule if we miss pilot targets by >15% for two consecutive weeks.

I’ll draft a short addendum language and upload to Drive; Marissa, can you incorporate commercial wording?

-Stephanie
Head of Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

---

From: Elena Moretti <elena.moretti@quanticai.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@quanticai.com
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 08:23:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA questions — TTFT and tokens/sec expectations

Thanks Michael and team — that proposed framing works for us for the pilot. A couple clarifying asks:

- Can you confirm whether TTFT numbers include TLS handshake and cold-start overheads (our mobile clients often see first-request TLS latency)?
- For the fallback model variant, please include a short note about any expected quality delta — specifically around hallucination frequency on summarization tasks.

We’re fine with pilot-scoped commitments and the proposed notification cadence. If you can confirm the TLS/cold-start behavior and add one sentence on expected quality delta in the addendum, procurement will approve quickly.

Appreciate it —
Elena

---

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moretti <elena.moretti@quanticai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA questions — TTFT and tokens/sec expectations

Elena — quick confirmations and next steps:

- TLS / cold-start: TTFT target excludes one-time client-side TLS handshake if that handshake is not reused for subsequent requests. We will instrument end-to-end from your sample client harness and report both network+TLS TTFT and server-only TTFT in the Console so you can see the breakdown.

- Quality delta for fallback variant: the variant we propose is a 4-bit quantized model optimized for throughput; in our internal tests for summarization it shows a modest quality delta (~3–5% lower ROUGE on your sample set) and slightly higher hallucination rates on long, under-specified prompts. We’ll include an explicit statement in the addendum and a requirement to run the pilot test set through both variants so Quantic can validate tolerance.

Action items:
1) Stephanie will upload the pilot addendum language to Drive (link above) by EOD Thu 8/16.
2) Karthik, please prepare the runbook steps to enable variant fallback and the Console dashboards to report TTFT breakdowns.
3) Elena, if procurement approves the pilot-scoped performance wording we’ll circulate the addendum for signature.

I’m tagging this as priority for the eu pilot.

Best,
Michael
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: quantic_pilot_requirements.pdf, Service_Levels_Draft_v2.docx
